h1:
Bangkok Mookata & BBQ Buffet
10 Good-Value Spots
intro: Mookata and grill-it-yourself BBQ buffets are the dinner Bangkok locals meet up for most often — sit around a hot grill, pick at the meat, talk for hours, and pay just a couple hundred baht each. We picked 10 spots that are open and genuinely busy, from budget buffets starting at a few hundred baht up to premium wagyu places, and we'll tell you straight who each one suits.

blocks.html: "Grilling" in Bangkok splits into two styles. The first is mookata — a domed grill with marinated pork on top and a moat of broth around the edge for blanching veggies and noodles, an easy, wallet-friendly Thai meal. The other is the Korean/Japanese BBQ buffet — a grate or butter grill with sliced pork and beef, plus Korean side dishes. Prices climb a little but still land in the low hundreds. This list covers both styles, ordered from best value to most premium.

blocks.text: 10 mookata & BBQ buffet spots Bangkok locals actually go to

items.name: Nene Korean BBQ Buffet
items.blurb: The cheapest entry point for Korean BBQ buffet on this list. The popular course is 299 THB and gets you pork belly, Korean side dishes and a ready-to-eat food line; the 499 course adds seafood, and 699 adds beef. Drink refills cost extra. A go-to for students and young office workers.
items.meta: Ratchada Soi 3 / Suan Phloen / The Mall Bangkapi

items.name: Best Beef
items.blurb: A well-known BBQ-and-pan buffet in the On Nut area. The draw is the choice of grills — butter grill, seafood grate, barbecue grill and a shabu pot — with quality grain-fed beef and pork, refilled freely for 2 hours. The course with drinks included costs a bit more. Walkable from BTS On Nut.
items.meta: Sukhumvit–On Nut (~400 m walk from BTS On Nut)

items.name: Bar B Q Plaza (buffet promo)
items.blurb: The mall chain almost everyone has tried, with its signature domed "Gon" pan grill. Usually à la carte, but the buffet promos make it much better value. Air-conditioned and comfortable, good for families or anyone who'd rather not sit at an open-air joint. Branches in nearly every major mall.

items.name: Saneh Mookata
items.blurb: An air-conditioned mookata spot in the Sukhumvit area, with fresh ingredients and a house dipping sauce. Good for anyone who wants mookata without the open-air smoke. More private than a roadside place, takes credit cards, and works well for groups or couples.

items.name: BBQ Resort
items.blurb: A BBQ buffet with a food line of more than 200 dishes — savoury, sweet and seafood. The standout is sheer variety, almost too much to choose from. Suited to big groups or big eaters. Several branches around Bangkok and the suburbs.

items.name: KoSiRae
items.blurb: A well-known Korean BBQ spot in the Thonglor area. The selling point is generous pork and loaded Korean side dishes, with bold, authentically Korean flavours. At the mid-300s it's good value for Thonglor. Long queues on weekend evenings, so go early or book ahead.

items.name: Mr.BBQ Korean Grill Buffet
items.blurb: A budget-friendly Korean BBQ buffet spread across malls and community malls. The focus is sliced pork, side dishes and a ready-to-eat Korean food line — good for a Korean-style meal on a lighter budget. The in-mall setting is easy to get to.

items.name: Mahanakhon Camping Mookata
items.blurb: A camping-themed mookata along Srinakarin Road. The draw is the outdoor-tent atmosphere and photo-friendly setting, great for groups who want food plus a vibe. The food is standard Thai mookata — come for the experience as much as the eating.

items.name: Sizzler (salad bar + mains)
items.blurb: Not mookata, but a grill-and-steak option in malls that plenty of people love. The highlight is the all-you-can-eat salad bar with bottomless veg, soup and bread; order a steak or grilled fish as your main. Good for anyone who wants grilled meat without doing the grilling themselves.

items.name: Premium wagyu BBQ buffet
items.blurb: The end of the road for beef lovers — an upmarket buffet around Sukhumvit serving premium Australian beef and unlimited wagyu, with over 30 side dishes and, at some places, late-night hours. Prices run into the high-500s. Best for a celebration or serious carnivores happy to pay more for quality.

blocks.title: How to pick a good-value spot
blocks.html: Check three things before you commit — the time limit (usually 90 minutes to 2 hours), whether drinks are included (many places charge ~50 THB extra for drinks), and the food-waste fee some places add if you don't finish what you took. Order a little at a time and refill — you'll get better value and avoid the fee.

blocks.text: Mookata vs Korean buffet — which to pick

blocks.html: If you want a relaxed Thai vibe, a long sit and a light bill, go for mookata — the domed grill comes with a broth moat for blanching veggies and noodles, so you get both broth and meat. Korean buffet suits anyone who loves sliced pork grilled on a grate, eaten with kimchi, fresh veg and Korean sauces — Korea-on-a-budget at a few hundred baht.

items: Lowest budget, a few hundred baht — Nene and Best Beef starter courses, great for students or big groups
Air-con, comfortable, in a mall — Bar B Q Plaza, Sizzler, Mr.BBQ, easy to reach near the BTS
Beef lovers / celebrations — Saneh Mookata and the premium wagyu buffet, worth paying more for quality
Big groups, lots of menu options — BBQ Resort, Mahanakhon Camping Mookata, good atmosphere

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: The prices listed are rough estimates. Buffet places change promos and courses often, so check the restaurant's page or call for the latest before you go — especially beef and seafood courses, where prices move with ingredient costs.

blocks.text: What to know before you go

items: Book ahead on weekend evenings — popular spots in Thonglor and On Nut get very long queues; arriving before 6pm is far easier
Check the time limit — most give you 90 minutes to 2 hours, and it's easy to run out of time before you're full if you're chatting
Cash vs card — mall restaurants all take cards, but some roadside mookata places are cash-only
Food-waste fee — many buffets charge if you take food and don't finish it, so order a little at a time

faq.q: How much does a BBQ buffet in Bangkok cost?
faq.a: Value spots like Nene or Best Beef start around 199–299 THB per person. Mall chains like Bar B Q Plaza run roughly 399–599 THB during buffet promos, while premium wagyu places climb to about 398–598 THB and up. Most prices don't include drinks, which are usually charged at around 50 THB extra.

faq.q: What's the difference between mookata and Korean BBQ buffet?
faq.a: Mookata uses a domed grill with a broth moat around it for blanching veggies and noodles — a relaxed Thai vibe at a light price. Korean buffet uses a grate or butter grill, focusing on sliced meat grilled and eaten with kimchi and Korean side dishes — bolder flavours and a slightly higher price.

faq.q: Which BBQ spots are near the BTS?
faq.a: The Sukhumvit branch of Best Beef is about a 400-metre walk from BTS On Nut. Saneh Mookata is on Sukhumvit 22, near BTS Asok/Phrom Phong. Bar B Q Plaza and Sizzler have mall branches near almost every BTS line.

faq.q: Do I need to book a BBQ buffet in advance?
faq.a: On weekend evenings, popular spots in Thonglor and On Nut have long queues, so book ahead or arrive before 6pm. Weekdays usually have more free tables, and mall restaurants you can just walk up and queue at.

faq.q: Is there a time limit on the buffet, and how long do you get?
faq.a: Most cap it at 90 minutes to 2 hours, though some premium places stay open late. Check with the restaurant first, and watch out for the food-waste fee many places charge if you take food and don't finish it.
